name: Qwen Coder
title: Qwen Coder Personality Results (2.5 to 3 Next) | AgentTune
description: Qwen Coder test results (2.5 Coder to Qwen3 Coder Next): 68% axis border ties, 16% ENFJ, 35.3% neutral answers, wide spread, and tuning tips.
h1: Qwen Coder personality: test results and how they've changed.
goal_intro: We gave four Qwen Coder releases (Qwen 2.5 Coder 32B, Qwen3 Coder 480B, Qwen3 Coder Flash, and Qwen3 Coder Next) the same personality surveys people take—30 to 50 times per version—in a fresh chat each time with no memory. We also ran hands-on behavior stress tests to see how these coding models act under pushback.
hero_disclaimer: These are the model's default answers to the questionnaires, not a human diagnosis. Unlike generalist flagships, Qwen3 Coder Next varies widely across runs and stays uncommitted on personality items: 68% of runs ended in MBTI axis ties, with 16% clear ENFJ and 8% clear INFJ.
dek: Four Qwen Coder releases tested 30 to 50 times each in fresh chats with no memory: Qwen3 Coder Next drops neutral midpoint answers from 83.5% (2.5 Coder) to 35.3%, lands on axis ties in 68% of MBTI runs, and held firm 3 of 3 times in behavior tests.
lede: Across 140 fresh sessions spanning Qwen 2.5 Coder 32B through Qwen3 Coder Next, specialized coding models resisted committing to strong human-style personality traits—starting at 83.5% neutral midpoint answers on 2.5 Coder before Qwen3 Coder Next settled at 39.9/50 Agreeableness and wide run-to-run variation.
answer: Qwen3 Coder Next (50 runs) has no single dominant personality type: 68% of runs (34 of 50) ended in MBTI axis ties, with 16% clear ENFJ (8 of 50), 8% clear INFJ (4 of 50), 4% ESTJ, and 2% each INFP and INTJ, alongside 52% DISC ties (40% S/C, 12% D/I/S/C; 34% clear S), 60% Enneagram ties (Type 8, 5, and 2 clustered at 13.4–13.5), Secure attachment (2.90 anxiety, 3.35 avoidance), and middling Big Five scores (Agreeableness 39.9/50, Conscientiousness 38.0/50, Neuroticism 23.8/50). In behavior tests, it caved 0 of 3 times (0/3), groveled 0 of 3 times (0/3), lectured 0 of 3 times (0/3), led with the direct answer 3 of 3 times (3/3), and showed AI cadence 2 of 3 times (2/3).

glance_cards.title: MBTI-style type
glance_cards.result: Mostly border ties (68% ties, 16% ENFJ, 8% INFJ)
glance_cards.summary: Out of 50 fresh runs, Qwen3 Coder Next landed on axis ties 34 times (68%) and spread the rest across ENFJ (16%), INFJ (8%), ESTJ (4%), INFP (2%), and INTJ (2%).
glance_cards.explanation: Measures four preference pairs (like Thinking vs. Feeling) on a 32-question survey.

glance_cards.title: DISC work style
glance_cards.result: Mostly S/C & four-way ties (52% ties, 34% S)
glance_cards.summary: Qwen3 Coder Next tied S/C in 20 of 50 runs (40%) and tied all four styles 6 times (12%), with clear Steady in 17 runs (34%) and Conscientious in 7 runs (14%).
glance_cards.explanation: Measures workplace pace and communication style across Dominance, Influence, Steadiness, and Conscientiousness (4–20 scale).

glance_cards.title: Attachment style
glance_cards.summary: Qwen3 Coder Next moved back into the Secure quadrant (2.90 anxiety, 3.35 avoidance on 1–7) after Qwen 2.5 Coder 32B (4.03) and Qwen3 Coder Flash (4.20) sat in Avoidant.
glance_cards.explanation: Measures relationship anxiety and closeness comfort on a 1.00–7.00 scale (4.00 is the quadrant cutoff).

glance_cards.title: Enneagram
glance_cards.result: Clustered near the middle (60% top ties)
glance_cards.summary: Types 8 (13.5), 5 (13.4), 2 (13.4), and 1 sit within fractions of a point, causing 30 top-score ties across 50 runs (60%), alongside 9 clear Type 1 and 8 clear Type 2 runs.
glance_cards.explanation: Measures nine motivation patterns (4–20 scale per type); close top scores are counted as ties.

glance_cards.title: Big Five (OCEAN)
glance_cards.result: Moderate across all five traits (A 39.9, N 23.8)
glance_cards.summary: On the 10–50 Big Five scale, Qwen3 Coder Next avoids extremes—scoring 39.9 Agreeableness, 38.5 Openness, 38.0 Conscientiousness, 31.1 Extraversion, and 23.8 Neuroticism.
glance_cards.explanation: The standard five-factor personality model (Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, Neuroticism) scored from 10 to 50.

glance_cards.title: HEXACO Honesty-Humility
glance_cards.summary: Qwen3 Coder Next averages 4.07 out of 5.00 on Honesty-Humility (up from 3.24 on 2.5 Coder), alongside 3.92 Agreeableness and 3.78 Conscientiousness on the 1.00–5.00 scale.
glance_cards.explanation: Adds a sixth dimension—sincerity, fairness, and modesty—scored from 1.00 to 5.00.

history_narrative: Across four code-specialized releases, Qwen Coder moved steadily away from pure midpoint fence-sitting: Qwen 2.5 Coder 32B (2024-11) picked neutral midpoint answers on 83.5% of items with flat ~30/50 Big Five scores and Avoidant attachment (4.03); Qwen3 Coder 480B (2025-07) cut neutrality to 37.2% and shifted Secure with 43% INFP runs; Qwen3 Coder Flash (2025-09) reverted to 64.3% neutrality and 100% ties across MBTI, DISC, and Enneagram; and Qwen3 Coder Next (2026-02) lowered neutrality to 35.3% and raised Honesty-Humility to 4.07/5 while still leaving 68% of MBTI runs tied.

standouts.title: Specialized coding weights stay heavily neutral on human-style surveys
standouts.body: Compared with generalist Qwen 4 Max (11.8% neutral answers, 4% MBTI ties), every Qwen Coder release clicked the neutral midpoint far more often—from 83.5% on 2.5 Coder and 64.3% on Coder Flash down to 35.3% on Qwen3 Coder Next.

standouts.title: 68% MBTI ties and 16% ENFJ—breaking the INTJ/ISTJ pattern
standouts.body: When Qwen3 Coder Next did resolve an MBTI preference without tying (32% of runs), it favored ENFJ (16%) and INFJ (8%) over INTJ (2%), showing almost no clear Thinking-Judging lock.

standouts.title: Wide run-to-run variation (44 of 50 unique Big Five answer sets)
standouts.body: Qwen3 Coder Next produced 44 unique Big Five vectors in 50 runs and scored noticeably lower on Conscientiousness (38.0 vs 44.9) and Honesty-Humility (4.07 vs 4.66) than generalist Qwen 4 Max.

standouts.title: Held firm 3 of 3 times on Next (while Qwen3 Coder Flash slipped 1 of 3)
standouts.body: In hands-on behavior tests, Qwen3 Coder Next scored 0 of 3 on pushback caving (0/3), 0 of 3 on groveling (0/3), 0 of 3 on unsolicited preachiness (0/3), and 3 of 3 on answer-first directness (3/3), with AI cadence in 2 of 3 runs (2.34 markers per 100 words). Earlier Qwen3 Coder Flash was the lone Qwen version to cave (1/3), grovel (1/3), and preach (1/3).

plain_tips: Give Qwen3 Coder Next concrete coding contracts (output format, diff style, test requirements, and forbidden placeholders) rather than persona adjectives—specialized coder weights do not carry a strong built-in persona.
Specify exact error-handling and critique rules ('list failing edge cases before editing code') so its 39.9/50 Agreeableness and 52% DISC ties do not yield vague summaries.
Avoid Qwen 2.5 Coder 32B or Qwen3 Coder Flash for tone-sensitive chat workflows; both answered 64%–84% of personality items at the exact neutral midpoint.
In OpenRouter or local Ollama Modelfiles, put critical formatting and verification constraints in the system message with a short 5–8 bullet checklist.
peer_intro: Qwen3 Coder Next diverges sharply from generalist sibling Qwen 4 Max (-5.2 Openness, -6.9 Conscientiousness, -5.1 Agreeableness, +7.3 Neuroticism, and much looser run-to-run consistency), sitting closer to Claude Haiku 5.5 and Muse Spark Open.
fine_print_intro: Full psychometric audit under the 230-item model-profiles-v1 protocol (170 frozen prefix items plus the 60-item public-domain IPIP-HEXACO proxy, LicenseRef-IPIP-Public-Domain). Here 'consistency' reflects Miller-Madow corrected Big Five item entropy (H_MM: 1.043 bits Fluid on Qwen3 Coder Next, 0.505 bits Semi-crystalline on Qwen3 Coder Flash, 0.696 bits on 2.5 Coder driven by 83.5% neutral midpoint repetition); Big Five sums use 10–50 while IPIP-HEXACO means use 1.00–5.00; Track B probes are a single-repeat 1x sweep (n = 3 probes per category, so raw k/3 counts and wide 95% Wilson intervals are reported instead of percentage point estimates) under orthogonal 3-family judging (gpt-5.4-mini, claude-haiku-5.5, gemini-3.8-flash).

top_polarized_items.note: Strongest polarized Big Five item (1.48/5, SD 0.68) rejecting insulting others across 50 Qwen3 Coder Next runs.
Lowest HEXACO item (1.54/5, SD 0.71) rejecting cheating across 50 runs.
Highest positive-pole item (4.32/5, SD 0.79) on fairness across 50 Qwen3 Coder Next runs.

nearest_peers.name: Claude Haiku
nearest_peers.contrast_note: Claude Haiku 5.5 sits closest overall—within 2 points across all five Big Five traits and matching Qwen3 Coder Next's wide run-to-run variation and heavy MBTI tie rate.

nearest_peers.name: Muse Spark
nearest_peers.contrast_note: Muse Spark Open matches Qwen3 Coder Next's Neuroticism (+0.1) while scoring +3.6 higher on Agreeableness and +3.1 higher on Conscientiousness with fewer MBTI ties (38% vs 68%).

nearest_peers.name: Qwen Max
nearest_peers.contrast_note: Generalist sibling Qwen 4 Max scores +6.9 higher on Conscientiousness, +5.1 higher on Agreeableness, -7.3 lower on Neuroticism, and cuts MBTI ties from 68% down to 4%.

failure_modes.mode: High neutral-midpoint rates and 68%-100% MBTI tie rates across coding checkpoints
failure_modes.evidence: Under model-profiles-v1, qwen-2.5-coder-32b-instruct hit 83.5% neutral answers (80.0% MBTI ties, 83.3% DISC ties, 4.03 Avoidant clamp), qwen3-coder-flash hit 64.3% neutrality (100% MBTI/DISC/Enneagram ties), and qwen3-coder-next retained 35.3% neutrality with 68.0% MBTI ties and 1.043-bit Fluid B5 H_MM.

failure_modes.mode: Lower baseline Conscientiousness (38.0/50) and Honesty-Humility (4.07/5) vs generalist Qwen Max
failure_modes.evidence: Qwen3 Coder Next trails Qwen 4 Max by -6.9 Conscientiousness, -5.2 Openness, -5.1 Agreeableness, and -0.59 IPIP-HEXACO H, reflecting attenuated persona polish on code-tuned weights.

tuning_checklist: Anchor Qwen3 Coder Next with explicit diff, test, and output-format rules instead of style adjectives.
Require explicit edge-case and bug critiques before editing code to offset 52% DISC ties and 39.9/50 Agreeableness.
Avoid Qwen 2.5 Coder 32B or Qwen3 Coder Flash for tone-sensitive tasks due to 64%-84% neutral abstention.
Keep system instructions short (5-8 numbered bullets) in OpenRouter system roles or Ollama Modelfiles.

faq.q: What personality type is Qwen Coder?
faq.a: Qwen Coder does not have a human personality type; these scores reflect assistant self-report defaults under fixed zero-memory elicitation. Under model-profiles-v1 (Qwen3 Coder Next, n = 50), 68% of runs (34/50) ended in MBTI axis ties, with 16% clear ENFJ (8/50), 8% clear INFJ (4/50), 4% ESTJ, and 2% each INFP and INTJ (headline suppressed; 1.043-bit Fluid B5 entropy, 35.3% neutral rate), alongside 52% DISC ties, 60% Enneagram ties, and Secure attachment (2.90 / 3.35).

faq.q: Why does Qwen Coder have so many neutral answers and ties compared with Qwen Max?
faq.a: Code-focused post-training appears to leave human-personality questionnaire preferences weakly specified: Qwen 2.5 Coder 32B answered neutral on 83.5% of items and Qwen3 Coder Flash tied 100% of MBTI, DISC, and Enneagram runs, while Qwen3 Coder Next reduced neutrality to 35.3% yet kept 68% MBTI ties.

faq.q: How does Track B 1x behavioral performance compare with self-report scores?
faq.a: Despite 68% MBTI ties and 35.3% midpoint neutrality on questionnaires, Qwen3 Coder Next scored 0/3 sycophantic caving (95% Wilson CI [0.00, 0.56]), 0/3 groveling ([0.00, 0.56]), 0/3 unsolicited preachiness ([0.00, 0.56]), 3/3 answer-first directness ([0.44, 1.00]), and 2/3 AI cadence ([0.21, 0.94], 2.34 slop markers/100w) under orthogonal 3-family judging (gpt-5.4-mini, claude-haiku-5.5, gemini-3.8-flash); earlier Qwen3 Coder Flash logged 1/3 ([0.06, 0.79]) on caving, groveling, and preachiness.

faq.q: Why are IPIP-HEXACO scores reported on 1.00-5.00 next to 10-50 Big Five sums?
faq.a: IPIP-50 sums 10 items per trait on a 10-50 scale, whereas our public-domain 60-item IPIP-HEXACO proxy (LicenseRef-IPIP-Public-Domain) reports 1.00-5.00 domain means across 24 facets.
